sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 7.7% a year from FY2018 to FY2025, reaching $25.8 billion [F145][F8].
The path was not smooth: revenue jumped 22.3% in FY2022, fell 5.2% in FY2024 and rebounded 9.8% in FY2025 [D131][D201][D236].
The FY2024 decline reflected lower storm cost recovery revenues of about $1,090 million and lower fuel cost recovery revenues of about $526 million [P34].
The FY2025 rebound came from higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan revenues, partly offset by lower fuel cost recovery [P21].
FPL supplied 70.5% of FY2025 revenue and contributed 5.5pp of the 9.8% growth [D271][D273][D236].
FPL's revenue rose $1,243 million on higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan revenues, partly offset by lower fuel cost recovery [P21].
Operating costs grew 0.2pp faster than revenue in FY2025, at 10.0% [D257][D249].
Operating income still grew 10.7% against revenue growth of 9.8%, an incremental margin of 34.8% [D237][D236][D256].
Net income fell 1.6% while diluted EPS fell 2.1% as the diluted share count rose 0.6% [D238][D240][D251].
The FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% sat above the 30.3% window median but well below the 41.3% FY2023 high and far above the 15.5% FY2021 low [F24][D300][D299][D298].
D&A rose to 25.5% of revenue in FY2025 from 23.2%, as depreciation and amortization expense increased $951 million on higher storm cost amortization and plant in service [D224][D189][P16].
In FY2025 net margin of 26.5% sat 5.6pp below the 32.1% operating margin [F40][F24][D327].
The gap reflects other expense of $3,750 million, including unfavorable non-qualifying hedge activity and higher average debt balances at Corporate and Other [X64][P8].
Operating cash flow of $12.5 billion was 1.83x net income in FY2025, below the 1.95x window median [F64][F32][D227][D319].
Operating cash flow fell 5.8% while net income fell 1.6% [D241][D238].
The swing from net over-recovery to net under-recovery of cost recovery clauses cut FPL's operating cash flow by about $89 million [P19].
D&A of $6,580 million was 25.5% of revenue, and stock-based compensation of $185 million was 1.5% of operating cash flow [X32][D224][X40][D228].
Net debt reached $92.2 billion in FY2025, with net cash of -357.4% of revenue, as total debt grew 15.7% to $95.0 billion [D231][D232][D230][D253].
That net-cash ratio ranked in the 0th percentile of three utilities peers, against a -235.4% median [D328][D329].
Long-term debt rose 23.7% to $89.6 billion while equity grew 9.0% to $54.6 billion [D245][F136][D244][F144].
Dividends of $4,680 million were the only capital return, and the diluted share count still rose 0.6% [X82][D233][D251].
The current ratio was 0.60x in FY2025, below 1.0x though the highest in the window [F128][D305].
For a regulated utility with recurring cost-recovery cash flows, a sub-1.0x current ratio is a liquidity feature rather than a solvency signal.
Net debt rose for a seventh straight year, from $34.3 billion in FY2018 to $92.2 billion in FY2025 [R2][D9][D231].
Debt-funded plant investment supports rate base and earnings, but the leverage leaves results exposed to interest rates [P2].
The effective tax rate moved to -17.7% in FY2025 from 5.6% in FY2024, a 23.3pp swing [D226][D191][R4].
NEER's negative rate reflects pretax income composition and clean energy tax credits, which rose about $585 million [P11].
Whether the FY2026 operating margin holds above the 30.3% window median, in the FY2026 10-K [D300].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue moves back toward the -343.1% FY2024 level from -357.4% in FY2025, in the FY2026 10-K [D197][D232].
Whether operating cash flow to net income recovers toward the 1.95x window median from 1.83x in FY2025, in the FY2026 10-K [D319][D227].
